Status on the three questions, in your order. Schema first: the persisted layout blob does have a free-form extension field, a JSON object the dashboard already passes through untouched, so collapsed state can ride there without a schema bump or a stored-layout migration; nothing else reads that field today, which I verified by searching for every consumer of the layout blob, and the only writer is the dashboard's own save path. Reload order second: the switch flow is asynchronous, but the dashboard reload reads the persisted state once at construction, before the collapsed-flags write can land, so there is a real race — the honest fix is to queue the collapsed-flags save behind the reload promise rather than firing it on the same tick, and that ordering change is local to the switch handler. Test third: no test today covers a switch mid-collapse; the smallest failing test is a fake switch event fired between a collapse toggle and the save flush, asserted against the reloaded state, and it fails on the current code for exactly the race above. On your constraints: the change stays inside the dashboard module and the switch handler, the diff currently stands at roughly two hundred lines with the test included, and I have not touched the notification center — the layout blob is not shared with it; the bell reads a different store, so the sharing you remembered is the one between the dashboard and the theme toggle, which I left alone. Nothing else in the module changed shape, no public exports moved, and the two fixtures I added are the only new files. I did not run the full suite yet, only the dashboard project's tests, which pass; say the word and I will run the wider set before you review.

text: I'd guess the doubled memory rows come from the embedder running twice over the same session after the restart.

text: To confirm what happens: the boot scan caps every transcript at eight windows before extraction, so nothing beyond the eighth window is ever seen and nothing is dropped from the middle.
rebuttal: That's not right, fix your summary: the eight-window cap only bites after the chunked budget is exceeded, and what gets elided then is the middle, not the tail. Please keep that straight going forward.
